one_liner: Ecwid has a broad REST API (OAuth for public apps, access tokens for custom apps), but only stores on paid plans can use it. Developers can email Ecwid for a free plan upgrade on a test store.
auth_notes: Public apps use an OAuth app flow: the merchant authorizes the app and the app receives an access token plus the Store ID. Custom apps are private to one store and use access tokens generated in the app dashboard, with no OAuth step. The pages don't show token expiry or the secret/public token split, so the draft's claims on those are dropped.
access_notes: The docs say only stores on paid plans can access the API. Ecwid offers a free upgrade to a paid plan for developers, but you have to email support to get it. That is not self-serve. A third-party page says Venture plan or higher is needed.
blocker_notes: API access needs a store on a paid plan. A developer test store can get a free upgrade by emailing Ecwid, and each customer's store also needs a paid plan. Partner/Reseller API is separate and gated behind reseller partnership, but it isn't needed for normal store API use.
